verdict.line: You lose if you trade into full Devour stacks near his tower or int fights before level 3; you win by forcing short trades off cooldowns and finishing with Stormbringer.

brief.thesis: Tahm Kench's entire kill pressure comes from stacking An Acquired Taste with Q (Tongue Lash) to set up a stun, but he has no way to force that trade if you don't stand still for it. Volibear's W (Frenzied Maul) and Q (Thundering Smash) both come off cooldown faster than his Q, so every short all-in you start after he's used Tongue Lash is a trade he can't answer. The 52.8% head-to-head over 282 games confirms this: Volibear wins the skirmish war even though the archetype as a whole sits near 48.8%.

theirWindow.when: He has 3 stacks and Q off cooldown
theirWindow.what: If he lands Tongue Lash at 3 stacks he stuns and consumes them, then can Devour you for free burst. Back off the moment you see the third stack flash, and don't walk into his 900-range tongue poke at that count.

yourWindow.when: His Q (Tongue Lash) just missed or is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: 5-6.5s is a long window at early levels. Close with E (Sky Splitter) to slow him in, then chain Q into W into W-refresh for the heal — he has nothing to punish you with until Tongue Lash resets.

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: 76.9% pick rate at 53.5% win; the extra sustain and mana regen let you spam W (Frenzied Maul) for poke without running dry before his Q cooldown resets.

boots.why: 48% pick rate, 57.9% win; the tenacity shortens how long his Abyssal Dive knock-up or Tongue Lash slow holds you still.

core.why: First item in the 68.8%-win build path; attack speed scales your Frenzied Maul refresh-heal loop.
Cooldown refund on crit shortens your Q and W windows, letting you re-engage before his Q resets.
Heal amp stacks with your passive and W heal, winning extended trades against his sustain.

situational.when: he's grouping with his jungler and you need the wave-clear proc to split push away from his Devour range
the game goes long and you need omnivamp to outlast his Thick Skin shield in extended skirmishes
you're ahead and want the active heal to win repeated short trades off his Q cooldown
he's building toward all-in burst with Devour and you need the damage-over-time conversion to survive the follow-up

runes.keystoneWhy: 34.6% pick at 51.1% win; the stacking attack speed rewards the short, repeated trades this lane wants — every auto between his Q cooldowns builds toward a faster Frenzied Maul loop.

summoners.why: 75.4% pick rate at 52.9% win; Ignite punishes his Thick Skin shield and Devour sustain by denying the heal-back, closing out the short trades this matchup is built on.

playing.title: Trade right after his Q
playing.detail: Tongue Lash is 7-5s depending on rank; the instant it whiffs or lands, start your combo — he has no stun or slow to answer with until it resets.

playing.title: Hold E for the engage
playing.detail: Sky Splitter's slow (16s cooldown) is what lets you actually catch him before he can walk away or wait out Thick Skin's passive shield buildup.

playing.title: Never fight at 3 stacks
playing.detail: The moment An Acquired Taste hits 3, he can stun you with Q and Devour for burst magic damage — disengage instead of trading.

playing.title: Use W's refresh heal to win extended trades
playing.detail: Casting Frenzied Maul twice on him deals bonus damage and heals you; this is how you out-sustain his passive health-based damage scaling.

playing.title: Save Stormbringer for the kill, not the engage
playing.detail: At 160-110s cooldown you only get a few casts per game; use it to finish a trade you already started, not to open one, since its 550 range still requires you to be close.

playing.title: Don't let him body-block for his team
playing.detail: His Devour can remove an ally from a fight; focus him down fast with your short-cooldown kit before he can set up a save elsewhere.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and win-rate figures are measured from live OP.GG data on the current patch (16.20.1); the tactical reasoning about cooldown windows and stack timing is this brief's own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid fighting Tahm Kench’s (Q). Close in and fight him whenever your skills come off cooldown. Use [E] to close in on him.
